channel.title: Bay Area Sports Blog
channel.description: Every Bay Area team, argued about properly. The 49ers, Warriors, Giants, A's and Sharks, written by a fan, not a network.

item.title: Jack Perkins Threw Six and Two Thirds Scoreless and They Lost Anyway
item.description: Rays 2, A's 1 on a walk off Tuesday night. Perkins gave up four hits and struck out eight, the lineup managed four hits of its own, and Kurtz, Rooker and Jacob Wilson are all on the 60 day.

item.title: Bryce Eldridge Is Him, and I'm Done Being Careful About Saying It
item.description: Eldridge homered in the first inning Tuesday in his best month of the year. He's 21, he's hitting .327 over his last 30 games, and he has the best OPS of any 21 year old in baseball.

item.title: Thirteen and a Half Over Miami and I Hate Every Half Point of It
item.description: The 49ers got ten days after Melbourne to get ready for Miami at Levi's. Stribling is out a month, Tonges' knee is a worry, and a 13.5 point line scares me.

item.title: They Sent Stribling Back Out on a Sprained Ankle. Fire the Training Staff.
item.description: The 49ers medical staff looked at De'Zhaun Stribling's ankle for a few minutes and sent him back in. Now he's out a month, and this has been going on for years.

item.title: Two Walk Offs, One 19 to 1 Beating, and I Watched Every Inning
item.description: A's 8, Mariners 7: Lawrence Butler's two run homer walked it off Sunday, Walton won Friday in ten, and a 19 to 1 Saturday sat in the middle of a series win.

item.title: The Padres Came Into Our Ballpark and Took All Three
item.description: Padres 6, Giants 4 finished a sweep at Oracle Park. Devers hit 36 and 37, Webb gave up six, and Wednesday's comeback over St. Louis feels like a month ago.

item.title: Raiders 27, Dolphins 13: Jeanty Twice, Paye Everywhere
item.description: Raiders 27, Dolphins 13: Ashton Jeanty scored twice, Kwity Paye had two sacks, and Kirk Cousins nearly gave it away with two picks in Week 1.

item.title: A's September Update: 60-88, Four Bats Hurt, and 7 of 10
item.description: Where the 2026 Athletics sit in mid September: 60-88, Nick Kurtz and Brent Rooker shut down, Henry Bolte and Gage Jump auditioning, and a ballpark that bends every number on the roster.

item.title: Giants September Update: 62-86, Devers at 36, Two Weeks Left
item.description: Where the 2026 Giants sit in mid September: 62-86, 28 and a half back, Rafael Devers at 36 homers, Bryce Eldridge hitting .270, and what the last two weeks are actually for.

item.title: 49ers Injuries From Melbourne: Stribling Ankle, Tonges MCL
item.description: Every 49ers injury from the 27-7 Week 1 win over the Rams in Melbourne: De'Zhaun Stribling's ankle, Jake Tonges' MCL, and the two cramp scares.

item.title: 49ers 27, Rams 7: The Best Night This Team Has Had In Years
item.description: 49ers 27, Rams 7 at the Melbourne Cricket Ground: Purdy's three touchdowns, the goal-line stand, the 99-yard answer and a defense that smothered Stafford.

item.title: 49ers at Rams, Week 1 in Melbourne: What Actually Decides It
item.description: A 49ers at Rams Week 1 preview from Melbourne: the defensive line injuries, the 3.5 point line on a neutral field, and what to watch at 5:35pm Pacific.

item.title: Alfred Collins Tore His Patellar Tendon and His Season Is Over
item.description: 49ers defensive tackle Alfred Collins tore his patellar tendon at Tuesday's practice in Melbourne and is out for 2026, two days before the Rams opener.

item.title: Three Solo Homers Was the Whole Night and Toronto Took the Series
item.description: Blue Jays 4, Athletics 2 in 92 degree heat at Sutter Health Park. Kazuma Okamoto hit his thirtieth and three solo homers were all the offense the A's had.

item.title: Jeff McNeil Hit a Ground Ball Sixty Feet and We Beat the Blue Jays
item.description: A's 6, Blue Jays 5 in Sacramento. Henry Bolte reached four times, Zack Gelof drove in two, Dylan Cease got beat up, Andres Gimenez tied it in the ninth and Jeff McNeil ended it with the bases loaded.

item.title: Two Swings and Landen Roupp Was All We Needed
item.description: Giants 2, Cardinals 1 at Oracle Park. Eldridge and Koss homered in back to back innings, Landen Roupp threw six shutout innings, and the ninth got scary anyway.

item.title: The Bullpen Gave It Back Twice and Devers and Eldridge Won It Anyway
item.description: Giants 5, Cardinals 4 in eleven innings at Oracle Park. Logan Webb went six, the ninth got away again, Rafael Devers and Bryce Eldridge kept dragging us back, and Shay Whitcomb walked it off.

item.title: The Quiet Part About the Yorks Is Getting Loud Around the League
item.description: League people are talking openly about 49ers ownership, the York family and a front office that lost its most important operator. What it means for 2026.

item.title: One Hit in Seattle, and Gage Jump Deserved a Lot Better Than That
item.description: Mariners 2, Athletics 0 at T-Mobile Park. Bryan Woo went eight innings on one hit, Gage Jump struck out seven in four and took the loss anyway, and the A's fall to 57 and 87.

item.title: Cesar Perdomo Gave Us Six Shutout Innings and the Eighth Took It Away
item.description: Mets 4, Giants 2 at Citi Field. Cesar Perdomo threw six scoreless, Jung Hoo Lee's two run single held up into the eighth, and then Carson Seymour gave up two homers in four batters.

item.title: Rafael Devers Is Carrying a 58 Win Team on His Back
item.description: Rafael Devers hit two more home runs and the Giants hit six in a 9-5 beating of the Mets at Citi Field. Since August 24 he is hitting .420 with 9 homers and 21 RBI.

item.title: Niners Landed in Melbourne and I Don't Know What Day It Is
item.description: The 49ers landed in Melbourne after a 15 hour charter flight and a 17 hour time difference, nine days before the Week 1 opener against the Rams at the MCG.

item.title: Two Hits. The Giants Got Two Hits in Pittsburgh and I Watched Every Pitch
item.description: Pirates 5, Giants 2 at PNC Park. Tidwell walked five, six Pittsburgh arms held San Francisco to two hits, and the season is functionally over at 58 and 83.

item.title: Bosa Practiced. Everybody Practiced. Now Get on the Plane.
item.description: Nick Bosa practiced fully for the first time since August 3, Kittle went a third straight day, Evans and Juszczyk returned, and the 49ers fly to Australia tonight.

item.title: Kittle Practiced. Bosa Didn't. Melbourne Is Nine Days Away.
item.description: George Kittle practiced and Nick Bosa did not, with both due out all three days. Mike Evans caught passes out of uniform and Puni cleared protocol.

item.title: The A's Have Five Hitters on the IL and deGrom One Hit What Was Left
item.description: Rangers 8, Athletics 1. deGrom allowed one hit over seven, Gage Jump gave up seven earned, and the five best bats in the organization are all hurt at once.

item.title: Giants 7, Braves 3, and This Team Has Quietly Been Fun for a Week
item.description: Devers opened it with his 30th, Molina went five with six strikeouts and no walks, and a four run sixth buried Atlanta. Five wins in the last eight.

item.title: Rafael Devers Hit Number 30 in Atlanta and I Would Like Some Apologies
item.description: Devers got to 30 homers in the first inning against Atlanta. Only the second Giant to do it since Bonds in 2004, on a 57 win team, after a summer of being called soft.

item.title: Eldridge Goes 4 for 5 With 4 RBI and the Giants Are Fun Again
item.description: Giants 7, Diamondbacks 2 in the nightcap. Bryce Eldridge matched career highs with four hits and four RBI, the first Giants rookie to do it since Posey in 2010.

item.title: They Ran Ron Wotus at the Lineup Card. The Game Hadn't Started Yet.
item.description: Ron Wotus got ejected during the lineup card exchange before Game 1 of the doubleheader against Arizona. Not in the third. Not in the ninth. Before the first pitch.

item.title: Vitello Got Run Again, and This Time He Took Logan Webb With Him
item.description: Two days after the six run ninth, Tony Vitello got thrown out in the third inning against Arizona, and Logan Webb got tossed with him. Five ejections. Fifty five wins.

item.title: 49ers 18, Raiders 12: A Kicker Won a Football Game
item.description: 49ers 18, Raiders 12 in the preseason finale. Eddy Pineiro went 6-for-6 including a 59 yarder and the defense allowed no touchdowns.

item.title: Bryce Eldridge Is Back, and Buddy Kennedy Is the One Who Paid for It
item.description: The Giants activated Bryce Eldridge off the bereavement list Thursday and designated Buddy Kennedy for assignment to make room. Eldridge is hitting .252 with 14 homers. Kennedy hit .121 in 33 at bats here.

item.title: Fire Tony Vitello. The Bullpen Is the Whole Case.
item.description: Reds 10, Giants 9 after a six run ninth. Twenty four saves in forty four chances. Same organization that had the fourth best bullpen in baseball last year. Enough.

item.title: Giants Blew a Six Run Lead in the Ninth and It Isn't Even Over
item.description: Nine to three going to the ninth. Then Eugenio Suarez hit a grand slam, the same Suarez Vitello got ejected screaming about in the first. I'm done with this season.

item.title: Bryce Eldridge on the Bereavement List: Take the Week, Kid
item.description: The Giants put Bryce Eldridge on the bereavement list on Monday. Nobody's said why and nobody has to. He'll be away about a week, and every other thing about this season can wait.

item.title: Rafael Devers Hit His 29th Homer and Nobody Said a Word
item.description: Devers went deep again Wednesday, three straight games, 29 homers on a 54-78 team. He gets called soft and not a winning player and I do not buy a second of it.

item.title: Vitello Ejected in the First Inning on a Check Swing
item.description: Tony Vitello got tossed in the top of the first on Wednesday for yelling get it right at a check swing call on Eugenio Suarez. Fourth ejection of his rookie year as a manager, and honestly, good.

item.title: The Warriors Spent All Summer Chasing a Star and Signed Georges Niang
item.description: Golden State's big summer ended with a 33-year-old corner shooter coming off a lost year. One year, $3.9 million, the fifteenth roster spot, and the second apron.

item.title: Jed York Arrested in Ohio: Two Misdemeanors and Nothing From the 49ers
item.description: 49ers owner Jed York was arrested Sunday morning in East Palestine, Ohio, pleaded no contest Monday to disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools, and the team has said nothing.
